title: A little lifting of the heart
word: A little lifting of the heart
hookLine: a small remembrance of God during the day is enough
tomorrow: what did a dying woman see when the room went dark?

cards: Two seconds between orders. Hands full, a line out the door, no chapel anywhere near. Does a glance toward God in a gap like that count for anything?
One of Brother Lawrence's letters answers, and the odd thing is who he pictures. Not a monk on his knees. Someone on the march, sword in hand.
Why would a kitchen brother write about prayer with a soldier in mind?

teach.b: Clue one, the size. Lawrence writes that a little lifting up of the heart is enough. A small remembrance of God.
One act of inward worship. Clue two, the place.
He says this holds even on a march, sword in hand. No candles, no kneeling, no hour set aside. The heart turns for a moment while the body keeps going.
So the soldier isn't a strange choice at all. He's the hardest case. If a prayer fits there, it fits in a kitchen, a classroom, a checkout line.
Prayers like these, he writes, however short, are acceptable to God. In the same letter he adds that they don't weaken a soldier's courage in danger; they strengthen it.

teach.h: THE MOVE UNDER THE WHOLE BOOK.
teach.b: Clue four, what the whole book leans on. A bare tree that showed a young man God's providence. A clumsy footman.
The same work with a new reason. A failure met without fuss. Underneath every one of them is this smallest move: a heart lifted toward God for a moment, and then again.
Catholics have an old name for prayers this short: aspirations. Today is our last day with Lawrence.

how: Catholics call very short prayers said in the middle of the day aspirations, or ejaculatory prayers: a name or a single line, said quietly while working.

games.q: what does “a little lifting of the heart” mean?
o: lifting your hands high during a church song
a feeling of happiness after good news arrives
a moment's turn of the heart toward God, mid-task

p: a moment's turn of the heart to God

s: a quick prayer is second best, a warm-up for real prayer
Lawrence calls such prayers, however short, acceptable to God.
he wrote that short prayers don't weaken a soldier's courage
in the same letter he says they strengthen it in danger.
Lawrence wrote that real prayer needs a long, quiet hour
he says a little lifting of the heart is enough, even on the march.

games.q: a nurse you know works twelve-hour shifts and says she never has time to pray. what would Lawrence's letter tell her?
o: save prayer for her day off; work hours don't really count.
a little lifting of the heart between patients is enough.
keep a prayer book in her pocket and read a page each break.
games.why: if a soldier on the march can lift his heart for a moment, so can a nurse in a hallway. short prayers, he writes, are acceptable to God.

practice: Stand and walk slowly for a minute, around the room or down a hall. Each time you pass a doorway or turn a corner, let your heart lift toward God for a moment, a glance rather than a speech, and keep walking.
Then sit for the rest of the time and wait for the next small lift to come on its own.

wordCard.voice: A little lifting of the heart. A moment's turn toward God, short enough for a march and, Lawrence writes, acceptable to God.

carryVoice: Keep this: a little lifting, then another, in the gaps between whatever comes next. Until tomorrow.
